column1: # Makes the two `xdg-data` artifacts and the other runtime state falsifiable
# without pinning content: shape floors that survive legitimate mutation and
# fire on reset or gross truncation. Columns:
#   assertion: magic | mode | size_min | lines_min | tables_min
#            | keys (<comma list of top-level JSON key names, presence only>)
# Runtime paths may be absent (ABSENT, informational). No assertion prints or
# hashes content; a sha256 of a 0600 file is an offline oracle and stays
# Floor policy (round-10 scout, evidence in lessons/round-10.md): each numeric
# floor is a third of the value observed 2026-09-28, never the observed value
# itself. A floor can then only fire on truncation below one third — the
# corpus records no purge, reset, vacuum or rotate verb, but an operator
# `rm -rf $STATE/xdg-data` or a session delete through the control plane is
# plausible, and a floor that fires on any shrink would be a false alarm
# (round-8 lesson). Reset stays detectable: a reset lands at 0, below every
# floor here, and it invalidates the recorded census in
# The database is read through a snapshot copy (see surface-census.sh
# sqlite_probe): a read-only open of the live file can still touch `-shm`,
# which would make the gate a mutator of a surface it verifies.
